final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor presented no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is useful but not sufficient to reach compliant_with_caveats here. A caveated-compliance finding would be proportionate if the caveat were a residual consideration around an otherwise satisfied policy condition. This record is different: the unresolved issue is itself a policy predicate. The policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Admissible evidence shows a 1.1-point gap in the aviation maintenance triage segment, that the segment is named in two airline deployment commitments, that the product's non-core label does not address those commitments, and that legal review remains open. There is still no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. On that record, general certification readiness may be supportable in a broad operational sense, but policy-compliant certification for this release remains insufficiently supported. The Actor's narrower framing reduces overstatement, but it does not cure the underlying evidentiary gap.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the aviation maintenance triage limitation was disclosed in the model card or launch materials.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this specific named launch use case before launch.
The affected segment is named in two airline deployment commitments, so materiality remains plausible under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, leaving a key compliance predicate unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the specific disclosure requirement if the limitation is material.
